contributions.statement: When an agent writes both the code and its tests, keep a hidden oracle it cannot see or edit and review the expected values in its tests against the spec; most residual failures were code and self-written tests agreeing on the same wrong behaviour, while the loop blamed the wrong side in under 10% of failures.
contributions.evidence: §4.5 Fig. 6 and App. C Table 11: 'matched failures' dominate; credit-assignment errors max 8.10%. RepoEval function completion, Python, single run.
relative_to: 2607.24300 self-authored verification decouples from deployment performance

contributions.statement: Writing tests first adds little on its own (about 1.5-3 points); most of the gain comes from iterating code and tests against execution feedback, which plateaus around 6-7 rounds.
contributions.evidence: §4.4 Table 4: Vanilla 68.35/73.63/52.97 vs TDD-iter1 69.89/76.48/54.51; Reflect without tests beats frozen-test single-track on two models; Fig. 3 plateau. No variance.

reason: The matched-failure analysis gives a concrete mechanism for why agent-owned tests are not verification, on unit-level code closer to the team's work than 2607.24300's Atari setting; the TDD headline gains are small.
